     Background

          World Bank publishes the World Development Report (WDR) as its annual flagship
            publication.

              First WDR: 1978

           Purpose:

               Provide in-depth analysis, data-driven insights, and policy recommendations

              Address global development challenges and promote sustainable development

          Each edition focuses on a specific theme critical for global development.

     Title/Theme of WDR 2026: “ThePromiseofArtificial
      Intelligence”

       Prepared by: World Bank team led by Gaurav Nayyar (Director)





World Development Report 2026                                                                                                           1

It is the first comprehensive assessment of what Artificial Intelligence
          Report – AI and
                                          (AI) means for 6.8 billion people living in low- and middle-income
          Developing Countries
                                    countries (LMICs).

                                       AI could help LMICs overcome development challenges that have
           Historic Opportunity
                                  remained unresolved for decades.

                               The Report addresses the scarcity of information on AI use in developing
         Knowledge Gap            countries, documenting how businesses and governments are using AI
                                and identifying obstacles to wider, productive adoption.

                                       AI is a General-Purpose Technology, comparable to steam power,
          AI as a General-Purpose
                                           electricity, computers and the internet, which can transform entire
         Technology (GPT)
                                 economies and societies rather than a single sector.

                               Steam power took about 80 years to reach lower-income countries,
                                            electricity 40 years, and the internet 20 years. In contrast, middle-
         Speed of AI Diffusion
                               income countries accounted for half of ChatGPT's global traffic within 6
                              months of its launch.

                                     Countries that benefited most from previous GPTs were not necessarily
         Lesson from Earlier GPTs  those that invented the technology; successful countries built
                                   foundations and rapidly developed applications on top of them.

          Risk of Inadequate         Countries that failed to invest in infrastructure, skills and institutions
          Preparation               benefited less and experienced greater disruption.

                                       AI has rapidly evolved from prediction to content generation across text,
          AI Evolution               audio and video, and now towards autonomous execution of complex
                                      tasks.

                                          AI's value for development depends on capabilities, concentration and
                                complements.
                                                 1.   Capabilities: AI can perform complex thinking tasks that guide
                                      decisions and often require human expertise, such as disease diagnosis,
                                 weather forecasting and agricultural advice. This can help address
                                    shortages of expertise in developing countries.
                                       2.  Concentration: Advanced AI models, their chips and data centres
         Three Factors             are controlled by a small number of companies in a few economies,
          Determining AI's           creating dependency risks and potentially limiting alignment with
         Development Impact      developing-country needs.
                                                                 ·   Opportunity from Concentration: Concentration can also benefit
                                    developing countries because they can customize existing AI models
                                      without spending billions of dollars developing the most advanced AI
                                 systems from scratch.
                                       3.  Complements: AI works most effectively where there is reliable
                                        infrastructure, strong education systems and capable institutions.
                                   Developing countries often face shortages in all three areas.





World Development Report 2026                                                                                                           2

AI needs to be adapted to local contexts because its performance is
          Local Customisation
                                shaped by the data on which it is trained.

                          How quickly countries develop the necessary complements and how
          Determinants of AI
                                          effectively governments and businesses reorganize to use AI productively
          Benefits
                                                 will determine the scale and speed of development gains.

                                            Earlier World Development Report 2016: Digital Dividends highlighted
         Analog + Digital
                                     the need for “analog complements” to digital technologies. AI requires
         Complements
                                  both strong analog and digital complements to realise its full benefits.

      AI Strategy for Developing Countries

                              Developing countries can benefit from AI through three pathways: Adopt,
                           Adapt and Advance. Each successive stage requires greater investment, skills
                          and infrastructure.
                                                        ·   Adopt Existing AI: Begin by adopting existing AI tools for practical
          AI Strategy for        applications such as helping doctors diagnose patients, improving farmers’
          Developing         crop decisions and increasing business productivity.
          Countries                     ·   Adapt AI to Local Needs: Adapt existing AI models to local languages,
                               laws, conditions and user needs. This is likely to deliver the biggest benefits
                                     for developing countries.
                                                        ·    3. Advance AI Technology: Build frontier AI models and supporting
                                 infrastructure domestically. This is the hardest and most expensive pathway.

                                                        ·   Requires advanced chips, large data centres, huge training datasets and
                               world-class AI researchers. Leading companies spend billions of dollars
                                    training frontier AI models.
                                                        ·    Feasibility of Frontier AI: For most developing countries, building frontier
                                  AI models is not a realistic near-term goal because only a handful of countries
                           and companies possess the necessary resources.
                                                        ·   Emerging Examples: India's Sarvam AI, UAE's Falcon and Sub-Saharan
                                 Africa's InkubaLM are examples of locally developed models designed to work
          Challenges of         better with local languages.
           Frontier AI                    ·   Need for Analog Foundations: AI adoption depends on strong foundations
                            such as reliable electricity, fast internet and basic education.
                                                        ·   Limits of Direct Adoption: AI systems trained in high-income countries
                        may perform poorly in different environments. In Nigeria, a system trained
                               using high-income-country data recommended excessive laboratory tests
                            because it learned medical norms more suited to Los Angeles than Lagos.
                                                        ·   Inclusive AI Delivery: AI solutions should account for different levels of
                               technology access. For people without smartphones or literacy, AI may need to
                           be delivered through voice calls on basic mobile phones.

                              Simply importing an AI model does not guarantee local effectiveness. Local
       Why Adaptation
                               adaptation can make AI more relevant and useful to developing-country
          Matters
                                 contexts.

                                  regional languages and needs.

                            Adapted models and AI coding tools can support medical-imaging systems for
           Practical
                                    clinics with few specialists, chatbots for small businesses and algorithms for
          Applications
                              monitoring government public spending.

                               Successful AI adaptation requires both digital and analog complements,
          Required
                                  including computing infrastructure, local-language data and workers with AI
         Complements
                                        skills.

                           The recommended approach is “Adopt and adapt, then advance”—use
           Overall Approach     existing AI first, tailor it to local conditions, and pursue frontier AI development
                                only where sufficient capabilities and resources exist.

     Doing in a Decade What Once Took a Century

         Doing in a Decade
                                   AI can potentially accelerate development by addressing shortages of highly

                                     skilled people in developing countries.
         Century

                                Developing countries often have too few doctors, business specialists,
             Skill Shortages         agricultural experts and skilled public officials to address complex problems
                            and improve services.

           Limitations of
           Traditional Capacity   Building expertise through education and training can take generations.
           Building

                        When adapted to local languages and context, AI can radically accelerate
          Role of AI              transformation by making expert knowledge accessible to millions, rather
                                than a small elite.

                                   AI can improve the productivity of millions of small businesses and farmers
         Economic Impact
                            and help overcome shortages of specialised expertise.

                                AI-supported weather forecasting systems have enabled some smallholder
           India – Agriculture     farmers to change behaviour in response to specific risks; some increased
         Example             farm expenditure by up to one-third, while others achieved net savings of up
                                   to $560 per farmer.

                                  Predictive AI analytics and decision-support tools can improve government
           Social Impact
                                  back-office administration and generate significant efficiency gains.

         Kenya – Judiciary     Kenya's judiciary used AI to assign 10,000+ court cases annually to 1,500+
         Example              mediators, helping reduce a significant case backlog.

                                   AI can strengthen transparency and accountability by detecting irregularities
            Political Impact
                            and supporting citizen oversight.

     Managing AI Risks

          Topic               Key Points

                                 Developing countries should be deliberate and proactive about AI—actively
         Managing AI Risks       exploiting its potential for enterprises, households and governments while
                              managing associated risks.

                                       Failure to actively adopt AI could cause developing countries to lose
          Risk of Inaction
                             economic dynamism and global relevance.

                                    AI is not yet replacing large numbers of jobs in most developing countries,
                                  but it is affecting some industries. Countries dependent on business
         Economic Risks
                               process outsourcing (BPO) such as call centres and back-office services
                                  face growing pressure as AI automates these activities.

                                    AI can become biased when trained on data that do not adequately
           Social Risks            represent local people, languages and cultures. It can also facilitate
                                  misinformation, fraud and cybercrime.

                             Advanced AI systems are concentrated among a small number of
            Political Risks          companies, mainly in the United States and China, creating risks of
                                    technological dependency for developing countries.

                                 Developing countries, like all countries, face risks arising from unintended
         Unexpected AI Risks
                                  or unexpected consequences of AI.

                                  Countries must continue investing in reliable electricity, internet access
         Analog Foundations    and strong education systems, which remain inadequate in many
                                 developing countries.

                                  Nearly one-third of rural schools lack reliable electricity; more than two-
         Sub-Saharan Africa –
                                     thirds lack dependable internet access; and nearly 9 in 10 ten-year-olds
          Foundation Gaps
                                cannot read a simple text.

                                 Developing countries should expand access to affordable computing
            Digital Building Blocks   infrastructure and create shared data resources, especially local-language
                                   datasets needed to adapt AI.

          AI Innovation          Governments should create a business environment supportive of start-
         Ecosystem             ups, enabling them to raise investment and experiment with AI applications.

                                    AI coding tools have made application development easier, resulting in
          Challenge of AI Pilots   thousands of pilot projects. The major challenge is determining which
                                   solutions actually work.

                              Governments and businesses need stronger evidence and capacity to test,
         Evidence & Scaling
                                   evaluate, procure and scale successful AI solutions.





World Development Report 2026                                                                                                           5

Public trust is essential for responsible AI adoption, particularly given limited
           Building Public Trust
                                  regulatory capacity and the rapid evolution of AI technology.

                              Governments should initially leverage voluntary standards covering impact
          Voluntary Standards    assessments, independent audits and testing protocols to promote
                                   responsible AI use.

                            Where voluntary standards are insufficient, governments should use
          AI Regulation            existing laws to address harms, while developing flexible AI regulations
                                       that avoid unnecessary barriers.

        Need for Immediate     Without adequate preparation, developing countries could miss AI's
          Action                  benefits while becoming increasingly exposed to its risks.

                             As of mid-2026, 80+ countries had published national AI strategies, but
          National AI Strategies
                                   only 1 of the world's 25 low-income countries—Rwanda— had done so.

                                  Countries with the most to gain from AI appear to be the least prepared,
         Preparedness Gap
                                      highlighting the need for accelerated policy action.

                                 Developing countries should not simply copy advanced economies' AI
           Different Priorities for
                                           priorities, which often focus on mass job losses or winning the frontier-AI
          Developing Countries
                                    race.

         Development-           Their priority should be using AI to increase productivity, strengthen public
         Focused AI Priorities    services and solve local development problems.

                                 Developing countries should avoid both AI hype and AI hysteria and pursue
         Balanced Approach
                                  adoption with care but without delay.

                             The recommended approach is “Adopt, adapt, and then advance” new
         Proven Path to
                                    technologies. This could help developing countries solve problems that have
          Prosperity
                                     resisted solutions for generations.

          Global Perceptions of   AI perceptions vary sharply across regions and among technology
          AI                   companies, citizens and governments.

         Technology               In the United States and Asia, technology executives generally view AI more
          Executives               positively and emphasise its potential.

                                         In the United States, Europe and Latin America, many citizens are
           Citizens' Concerns     concerned about white-collar job automation, energy demand, algorithmic
                                  bias and data privacy.

                                    African policymakers tend to occupy a middle position—enthusiastic about
          African Policymakers   AI's potential to improve public services, but concerned that it could widen
                                 the digital divide.

                                    AI can help small businesses grow through tools such as mobile
         Economic Impacts –
                              messaging-based marketing advice, but automation of call centres can
          Opportunities & Risks
                                  displace workers and narrow traditional paths to economic growth.

           Social Impacts –         AI can improve government service delivery and learning in public
          Opportunities & Risks   schools, expanding access to knowledge; however, embedded bias in

government decision-making can harm people.

            Political Impacts –       AI can increase voice and agency, but malicious actors can use it for
          Opportunities & Risks   disinformation, privacy violations and cybercrime.

                                Evidence remains evolving. Thousands of AI applications and pilots in
         Evidence on AI          agriculture, health and education show benefits, but definitive evidence of
          Impacts              economy-wide improvements in growth, job quality/quantity and large-

                                 systems.

      AI as a General-Purpose Technology (GPT)

          AI as a General-       A General-Purpose Technology (GPT) is characterised by widespread use,
         Purpose Technology    continuous innovation and the ability to stimulate complementary
         (GPT)                  innovations across industries. AI fits all these characteristics.

                                         In a few years, AI has evolved from predictive machine-learning
           Evolution of AI          algorithms → Large Language Models (LLMs) generating text, audio and
                                  video → AI agents capable of autonomously executing a series of tasks.

         Continuous              AI capabilities are improving rapidly and continuously across increasingly
         Improvement          complex tasks.

          Competition-Level       AI progressed from being well below top human performance to human
         Mathematics            parity in competition-level mathematics within only a few years, 2021–24.

                                     AI performance on PhD-level science questions reached human parity
          PhD-Level Science
                                   within one year (2023–24).

           Predictive →
                                        AI's evolution from predictive to generative to agentic systems has
          Generative → Agentic
                               produced innovative applications across multiple sectors.

                                     AI has enabled applications in medical imaging, weather forecasting,
          AI Applications
                                 personal tutoring and many other fields.

         Development               1.   AI's role in development can be understood through capabilities,
        Mechanism – 3 Key      concentration and complements.

                                      capabilities and their ab

      Capabilities of AI

                                     AI is “an umbrella term for a set of loosely related technologies” that
           Capabilities of AI        supports non-routine cognitive and analytical tasks requiring judgment,
                                    contextual understanding and problem-solving.

                                        Particularly valuable where capabilities for cognitive tasks are scarce,
         Relevance to
                                   costly or undersupplied, such as shortages of teachers and healthcare

                                    professionals.

                             Used for summarising information, writing, data analysis, translation,
          AI in Businesses
                              customer interaction and software development.

                             Used for resource allocation, citizen alerts, forecasting, improving
          AI in Governments
                                      frontline services and virtual assistants for citizen engagement.

                                                             ·   Enables less-experienced workers to perform more advanced
                                   cognitive tasks, shifts some work away from scarce specialists and
                                   increases the productivity of existing workers.
                                                             ·   Pathway 1 – Leveling Up: When AI automates more expert tasks within
                               an occupation, it can lower entry requirements for performing that work.
                                 Evidence exists in customer support, professional writing and software

         Shortages                         ·   Pathway 2 – Task Shifting: AI can shift cognitive tasks to adjacent
                                occupations employing workers with less expertise; e.g., medical-image
                                  screening can move from scarce specialists to lower-level healthcare
                                     providers.
                                                             ·   Pathway 3 – Productivity Enhancement: AI makes people more
                                   productive in their existing roles. Generative AI can support teachers

          Negative Effects –
                                     AI can eliminate some jobs and increase inequality, including potential
         Employment &
                                 displacement of call-centre workers.

                                  using AI to create deepfakes, while malicious actors can use it for

                                    cyberattacks.

                                weaker.

            Electricity                countries.

                                  Excessive dependence on AI can weaken human skills. In classrooms, early
          Cognitive Offloading    signs show students allowing AI to perform some thinking and learning
                                   they would otherwise do themselves.

                                     AI may reduce demand for entry-level workers, particularly in areas such

                                as software services, thereby reducing opportunities for on-the-job

                                     AI systems largely designed in high-income countries may not adequately

                                                        fit developing countries' cultures, laws, languages and social norms.

                                     AI is spreading globally faster than previous general-purpose
          AI Diffusion             technologies, creating an opportunity for developing countries to
                                    accelerate development and catch up with wealthier countries.

                               Lower-income countries adopted the steam engine about 80 years later,
           Historical Adoption
                                          electricity about 40 years later, and computers/internet about 20 years
         Lags
                                        later compared with high-income countries.

                                   At launch in November 2022, more than 70% of ChatGPT user traffic
         ChatGPT Diffusion       originated from the United States; within 6 months, middle-income
                                    countries collectively accounted for 50% of traffic.

                             By April 2025, ChatGPT adoption among internet users averaged nearly
          AI Adoption Gap      25% in high-income countries, compared with 5.8% in upper-middle-
                               income, 4.7% in lower-middle-income and 0.7% in low-income countries.

                                 Rapid AI diffusion creates a major opportunity for developing countries to
         Development
                                catch up in living standards, but large differences in usage intensity mean
          Opportunity & Risk
                                     AI benefits could initially remain concentrated in higher-income countries.

     Concentration of AI

                                     AI capabilities depend on a value chain concentrated in a handful of
          Concentration of AI      countries, covering AI models, data centres, semiconductors, large
                                   datasets and specialised talent.

                              Most leading publicly listed AI companies are based in the United States
          Leading AI Companies
                                   or China; prominent private AI companies are also concentrated there.

                                   Concentration creates agglomeration effects: specialised talent attracts
          Agglomeration Effects   firms and venture capital, which fuels research and start-ups, attracting
                               even more talent and investment.





World Development Report 2026                                                                                                           9

The concentration creates a cycle that enables efficient matching of top
           Self-Reinforcing Cycle   talent with leading firms and leading firms with capital, making it
                                     increasingly difficult for followers to catch up with the AI frontier.

                             The San Francisco Bay Area maintains its position as the leading global AI
          Leading AI Hub
                                 hub.

                                   Concentration of key AI building blocks—advanced models, computing
                                     infrastructure and specialised hardware—in a few companies and
         Dependency Risk
                                    countries can make developing countries dependent on technologies they
                             do not control.

                                   Concentration also creates an opportunity: developing countries can
          Opportunity from
                               customise existing AI models for local contexts without spending billions
          Concentration
                                     of dollars building advanced systems from scratch.

          Application-Based      Developing countries can build useful AI applications on top of existing
         Approach             models rather than developing the underlying frontier models themselves.

                             The cost of using advanced LLMs such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
            Falling AI Costs
                                has declined considerably.

          Open/Freely Available   Several LLMs are freely available or open for modification, including
         Models                 Apertus, DeepSeek, Falcon, Gemma, Kimi, Mistral, Llama and Qwen.

                              These models can be downloaded, adapted to local languages and needs,
          Local Adaptation
                              and used to create new applications.

                                      Building applications on existing/open models allows developing countries
         Lower Entry Barrier       to innovate without requiring massive investments in computing power,
                                 data or highly specialised talent.

                                     AI concentration creates both dependency risks and development
                                    opportunities. The practical strategy for developing countries is to leverage
           Overall Message
                                       existing AI capabilities and adapt them to local needs rather than
                                  immediately attempting to compete at the frontier.

     Complements

                                      AI capabilities can have immediate effects, but their full potential will be
         Complements
                                       realised only as analog and digital complements improve.

                                      AI tools are becoming easier to use and customise; people without formal
         Ease of AI Access         technical skills or expensive hardware can access AI advice through local-
                                language chatbot prompts on smartphones.

                                   Enable people with little or no programming experience to build
          AI Coding Assistants
                                       applications using everyday language instead of computer code.

                                             Full productive potential of AI depends on widespread infrastructure,
          Required Complements    skills, data systems, a good business environment and institutions,
                            among other factors.

     Promise and Peril of AI

                                 Through adoption, adaptation and advancement, AI is transforming
         Promise and Peril of AI
                                         national well-being across economic, social and political dimensions.

                                        AI affects what people do and how much they earn, restructuring
         Economic Impact
                                     growth, increasing productivity and transforming jobs.

     Long-Term AI Impact

         Long-Term AI Impact on     With the right complements, AI can enable transformative
